answer: The haven holds work receipts rather than names, so the plume of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, burned when the recruit misbehaves, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the pulse of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
